data.note: CME first seen to the NW by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-012T08:23Z, as well as to the North by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not seen in SOHO LASCO in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-12T04:35Z. The source of this event is likely far sided, and is seen as field lines opening along or just beyond the West limb (approx. N15W157) in STEREO A EUVI 195 and from beyond the North limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at approx. 2026-08-23T07:45Z.

data.note: CME first seen to the East in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-14T05:09Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME was not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-14T04:48Z. The source of this event is a filament eruption centered at approx. S10E20 with liftoff beginning at approx. 2026-08-14T04:00Z. This filament is heavily deflected to the West as it erupts as seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

data.note: CME first seen as a halo to the SE by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-08-14T07:38Z, as well as by GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME was not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap which began at 2026-08-14T04:48Z. The source of this event is a C4.1 flare from Active Region 14503 (S17W57) seen peaking at 2026-08-14T07:01Z in SDO AIA 131. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 94, 171, 193, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the W in STEREO A COR2 and as a NE partial halo in GOES CCOR-1, not seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to DSN gap, but imagery became available with later backfill. The source is far-sided, only likely visible as field line movement over the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 starting as early as 2026-08-14T10:42Z and over the NE limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 starting around 2026-08-14T10:55Z. This CME is preceded by a faint front that is quickly overtaken by the main bulk of this CME.

data.note: CME first seen to the W in STEREO A COR2 starting at 2026-08-14T18:23Z. It is also seen to the W in GOES CCOR-1. In real time, this CME is covered by a data gap in SOHO LASCO C2/C3. The source of this CME is most likely related to moving field lines seen beyond the W limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-08-14T17:18Z. An eruption that may be related can be seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 near former AR 14505 (located approximately N15W145) beginning around 2026-08-14T16:55Z.

The majority of the CME is obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. A possible source is a small filament eruption beyond the N limb best seen in GOES SUVI 304 starting at 2026-08-14T21:52Z.

data.note: This CME is visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery and to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery before a real-time data gap starting around 2026-08-15T04:24Z. This CME is not yet visible in SOHO LASCO C3 due to the aforementioned data gap. In GOES CCOR-1, there is an Earth-shine imaging artifact obscuring the initial view of the CME, but is likely seen to the NE following the imaging artifact. There is no clear source for this CME, but it is believed to be far sided. This CME follows in the same path of the CME first seen in SOHO LASCO C2 imagery starting at 2026-08-14T22:24Z.

The source may be related to some fluctuation in filament structures seen near the E limb in SDO AIA 304 for several hours before and after the CME start time, but no clear filament liftoff can be seen.

There is no good source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This is consistent with measurements.

It is also seen to the NNE in SOHO LASCO C3 but is not seen in STEREO A COR2 and is mostly obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. There is no definitive source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This feature partially overlaps with CME: 2026-08-15T07:24Z.

There is no definitive source candidate on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This is consistent with measurement.

The majority of this CME was missed in real time by SOHO LASCO C3 due to a data gap between downlinks. This CME is associated with a C8.2 class flare from AR 14506 (N10W42) that peaked at 2026-08-16T19:28Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131.

data.note: CME visible to the NW in GOES CCOR-1 and the NE in STEREO A COR2. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a gap in the DSN. The source is likely an eruption from AR 14506 (approximately N12W51) or AR 14510 (approximately N13W64). The eruption from AR 14506 may be the most likely candidate, starting around 2026-08-17T04:52Z with dimming and post-eruptive arcades best seen in SDO AIA 193. The eruption is also seen in STEREO A EUV 195/304.

The source is not found in available EUV imagery, and is likely beyond the East limb from the point of view of SDO AIA imagery.

This CME is associated with the M8.1 flare from Active Region 14513 (N05E80) peaking at 2026-08-20T11:42Z as seen in SDO/AIA 131, 193, 171, and 304. Associated moving/opening field lines are visible to the E/NE in SDO/AIA 193 and 171, as well as filament material in SDO/AIA 304. These features are additionally visible in GOES SUVI wavelengths.

The source may be related to a small eruption from AR 14513 (N04E66) best seen in SDO AIA 304 beginning around 2026-08-21T06:24Z.

data.note: This CME is visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 before a data gap, to the NW in GOES CCOR-1, and as a halo with the bulk portion directed to the W/NW in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source for this CME is a long duration M1.6 flare from Active Region 14507 (N04W88) as seen in SDO/AIA 131 with associated moving/opening field lines visible in SDO/AIA 193, 171, and GOES SUVI 284. Other source features include an EUV wave best seen in SDO/AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 284, brightening in STEREO A EUVI 304, and dimming in STEREO A EUVI 195. Post eruptive arcades are visible in all main wavelengths from SDO/AIA, GOES SUVI, and STEREO A EUVI. These various source features are visible starting as early as 2026-08-21T09:00Z through 2026-08-21T12:12Z.

The source may be outflow or continued field line movement following CME: 2026-08-21T09:36Z, potentially observed as field line movement over the NW limb in GOES SUVI 284 spanning approximately 2026-08-21T11:00Z to 2026-08-21T17:00Z following the main eruption responsible for CME: 2026-08-21T09:36Z.

An opening of field lines is visible over the western limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/193/284 imagery around this time, with dimming visible in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery.

data.note: Thin, fast CME observed to the W in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not observed in STEREO A COR2 likely due to its occulting disk. The source is AR 14514 (S10W83), with field line movement followed by a post eruptive arcade observed in SDO AIA 171/193 near the SW limb, centered approximately ~S13W90 (but may vary W80-W100), starting around 2026-08-22T23:47Z. Also observed brightening, field line movement, and slight dimming from this region in STEREO A EUVI 195/304.

This front has a more faint nose and a brighter piece following it; this preliminary analysis captures both in one measurement. Longitude W90 is used as a reasonable approximation and not a plane-of-sky, but could vary W80-W100.

data.note: CME visible to the west in STEREO A COR2 only. The source may be an eruption best seen as dimming starting at 2026-08-23T17:35Z in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery around N10W115.

data.note: CME visible to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 imagery. The CME is not clearly visible in GOES CCOR-1 or STEREO A COR2 imagery. No clear source for this CME is found, and it may originate from beyond the east limb of available EUV imagery. Faint opening field lines are visible off the NE limb around 2026-08-23T20:00Z in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA.

data.note: CME visible to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The potential source is not clear, and may be one of several eruptions seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery spanning from latitudes N00 to N10 and longitudes N120 to approximately N135 starting as early as 2026-08-23T17:35Z with dimming and post-eruptive arcades.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location. The leading edge of the CME is not clearly measurable in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery.

data.note: CME visible to the NW in STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is partially obscured by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The CME is not visible in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real-time due to a data gap. The source is likely an eruption seen around N10W120 in STEREO A EUV 195/304 starting at 2026-08-24T09:25Z. Dimming and post-eruptive arcades are best seen in STEREO A EUV 195. Moving field lines are also visible on the NW limb in SDO AIA 171/193 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the potential source location using STEREO A COR2 imagery. The leading edge of the CME was not clearly measurable in GOES CCOR-1 imagery.

An eruption is visible beyond the limb in STEREO A EUV 304 imagery starting around 2026-08-24T12:45Z. Moving field lines are also visible in STEREO A EUV 195.

data.note: CME first seen to the Northwest by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-08-24T20:36Z. This CME is blocked by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap from 2026-08-24T19:09Z to 2026-08-24T23:38Z. The source of this event likely originates beyond the Western limb as field line opening is seen in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284 beginning at 2026-08-24T19:46Z from beyond the NW limb.

data.note: Faint, slow CME first seen to the NE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-08-24T22:36Z, as well as by STEREO A COR2 in later frames. The source of this event is a gradual M1.7 flare from Active Region 14513 (N03E13) seen peaking at 2026-08-24T19:36Z. Field line opening and Westward moving dimming is seen in SDO AIA 193 in association with this flare, likely suggesting Westward deflection.
